title: qsort with a Python callback
description:
Let C call back into Python to sort an array.

```
before: [5, 1, 4, 2, 3]
after:  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
comparisons made: 8
```

starter.main.py:
import ctypes
import ctypes.util

libc = ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("c"))
values = (ctypes.c_int * 5)(5, 1, 4, 2, 3)

# TODO
print(list(values))

hints: Inside the callback, `a = ctypes.cast(pa, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int))[0]` reads the value (lesson 6.04).
`(a > b) - (a < b)` is the comparison result C expects.
requirements: Declare the callback type with `ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)`.
Build a `(ctypes.c_int * 5)` array and pass it to `libc.qsort`.
Count the comparisons; keep a reference to the callback while C may still call it.
stretch: Sort an array of `Point` structs by `x`.
